previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. Thompson was admitted with atypical chest pain and a history of coronary artery disease, mechanical aortic valve, and recent urosepsis. Initial evaluation ruled out acute myocardial infarction with normal troponins and EKGs. Telemetry revealed frequent premature ventricular contractions (PVCs) correlating with his symptoms. A Persantine MIBI stress test showed no evidence of ischemia but confirmed fixed defects from prior infarcts and a reduced ejection fraction of 34%. EP adjusted his pacemaker settings to reduce PVC burden, and he was encouraged to adhere to metoprolol therapy. His chronic issues, including C. difficile on oral vancomycin, nephrolithiasis with hematuria, and therapeutic INR on warfarin, were managed. He improved symptomatically and was discharged home with services for follow-up with cardiology, EP, and urology, along with outpatient echo and medication reconciliation.

pressors (norepinephrine), which were discontinued on HD2. 
He was then transferred to the floor on only cefepime. As 
sensitivities returned as GNR (Klebsiella Pneumonia) he was 
transitioned to Ciprofloxacin PO given similar bioavailability 
of PO and IV cipro for bacteremia. He improved and was afebrile. 
End date of abx is ___ for a total of 2 weeks.

# ELEVATED INR: supratherapeutic, with INR of 4 on admission.  
Held warfarin initially and INR normalized. He was later 
restarted on warfarin but with the antibiotics INR was elevated. 
Warfarin dose was decreased from 6mg to 4mg and on discharge INR 
had downtrended to 2.9

INDICATION:  History: ___ with history known kidney stone  p/w fever,
weakness, and l flank pain  // pleave eval stent placement and stone placement

TECHNIQUE:  MDCT axial images were acquired through abdomen and pelvis
following intravenous contrast administration with split bolus technique.
Coronal and sagittal reformations were performed and submitted to PACS for
review.
Oral contrast was administered.

DOSE:  DLP: 800.7 mGy-cm (abdomen and pelvis.

COMPARISON:  Comparison is made to outside CT from ___ (___
___), and prior abdominal ultrasound from ___.

FINDINGS:



LOWER CHEST:

There are miniscule bilateral pleural effusions (2:5), and minimal adjacent
atelectasis. The heart is moderately enlarged.  Partially visualized pacer
leads are unchanged in position. Left ventricular calcifications are also
unchanged (02:10).  There is a small hiatal hernia.

ABDOMEN:

GENERAL: There is no intra-abdominal free air or free fluid.

HEPATOBILIARY:  The liver contour is nodular, and there is relative
hypertrophy of the left lobe of the liver, as described on prior abdominal
ultrasound. A punctate calcification is noted in the right hepatic lobe
(02:23), possibly from prior granulomatous infection.  There is no
intrahepatic biliary ductal dilatation.  A focal hypodensity in the left
hepatic lobe is subcentimeter in size (02:13), too small to characterize.. 
The gallbladder is nondistended, with multiple calcified gallstones (02:29).
PANCREAS: The pancreas has normal attenuation throughout, without evidence of
focal lesions or pancreatic ductal dilatation.  There is no peripancreatic
stranding.
SPLEEN:  The spleen shows normal size and attenuation throughout, without
evidence of focal lesions.
ADRENALS:  The right and left adrenal glands are normal in size and shape.
URINARY: Since the prior CT, there has been interval placement of a double-J
stent, coursing through the right ureter, with appropriate pigtail all a G in
the bladder (2:71). In the proximal left ureter, there is re- demonstration of
a calcified stone, which measures 9 mm in maximal diameter (02:34). The degree
of hydronephrosis in the right kidney has improved since the prior outside CT.
Stable appearing nonobstructing staghorn calculus in the lower pole of the
left kidney is again, with unchanged appearance of a simple cyst in the upper
pole of the left kidney (02:24). There is no hydronephrosis on the left. 
There is mild perinephrourteral fat stranding on the left, which also extends
along the course of the iliac vessels.
GASTROINTESTINAL:  Small bowel loops demonstrate normal caliber, wall
thickness and enhancement throughout.  Diverticulosis of the sigmoid colon is
noted, without evidence of wall thickening and fat stranding.. Appendix
contains air, has normal caliber without evidence of fat stranding.
RETROPERITONEUM:  There is no evidence of retroperitoneal and mesenteric
lymphadenopathy.
VASCULAR:  There is mild focal ectasia of the infrarenal abdominal aorta, just
above the level of the bifurcation, measuring up to 2.5 cm in maximal ___
posterior dimension (02:37).  There is moderate calcium burden in the
abdominal aorta and great abdominal arteries.

PELVIS:

The urinary bladder is underdistended, but there is no evidence of wall
thickening or mural nodularity. There is no evidence of pelvic or inguinal
lymphadenopathy.  There is no free fluid in the pelvis.



BONES AND SOFT TISSUES:

There is no evidence of worrisome lesions. Abdominal and pelvic wall is within
normal limits.  Multilevel degenerative changes are noted in the lumbosacral
spine.

IMPRESSION:



1. Indwelling right double-J ureteral stent in appropriate position, with
improved degree of hydronephrosis in the right kidney, and persistent 9 mm
proximal right ureteral stone, now slightly more distal in position compared
to the prior study from ___.
2. Left lower pole staghorn calculus is nonobstructing, and unchanged since
the prior study, measuring up to 1.9 cm.
3. Mild left nephroureteral fat stranding also tracks along the left iliac
vessels, and is non-specific, possibly infectious or inflammatory.  Correlate
clinically with possible presence of pyelonephritis. Also correlate with any
related prior recent procedural history.
4. Nodular liver, with relative hypertrophy of the left hepatic lobe,
compatible with underlying hepatic fibrosis/ cirrhosis, as seen on prior
ultrasound.
5. Cholelithiasis, with no evidence of cholecystitis.
6. Focal ectasia of the infrarenal abdominal aorta is stable.
7. Moderate cardiomegaly and small hiatal hernia, with miniscule bilateral
pleural effusions.

NOTIFICATION:  The above findings and changes to the initial wet read
regarding IMPRESSION #3 were discussed via telephone by Dr. ___ with Dr.
___ on ___ at 11:37 ___, following attending review.
